level1.question: Ano ang tawag sa alpha-numeric code na ibinibigay sa bawat PER application sa System para sa tracking purposes?

choices.A: Electronic Reference Number
choices.B: PER Control Number
choices.C: OMS Tracking Code
choices.D: Application ID Number

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 3.4, ang Electronic Reference Number ang alpha-numeric code na ibinibigay sa bawat application sa System para sa tracking purposes.

level1.question: Aling ahensya ang responsable sa hosting at maintenance ng OMS at PMS, pati na rin ang subscription ng cloud services?

choices.A: Bureau of Customs
choices.B: DTI
choices.C: ECD
choices.D: DTI-EMB

level1.reason: Sec. 4.1.1 ay nagsasaad na ang DTI ang responsable sa hosting at maintenance ng OMS at PMS, kasama ang subscription ng cloud services.

level1.question: Sino ang may administration ng PMS, kasama ang paggawa at pamamahala ng user access?

choices.A: DTI
choices.B: DTI-EMB
choices.C: Bureau
choices.D: MISTG

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 4.1.2, ang administration ng PMS ay nasa Bureau, kasama ang creation at management ng user access.

level1.question: Ano ang GSP (Generalized System of Preference) ayon sa CMO 06-2025?

choices.A: Bilateral na kasunduan sa pagitan ng dalawang bansa
choices.B: Multilateral na regional trade agreement
choices.C: Reciprocal na kasunduan ng ASEAN countries
choices.D: Unilateral na scheme kung saan ang developed countries ang nagbibigay ng customs duty preferences

level1.reason: Sec. 3.8 ay naglalarawan sa GSP bilang unilateral na scheme kung saan ang customs duty preferences o concessions ay ibinibigay ng developed countries.

level1.question: Ilang working days ang itinakdang panahon para matapos ang application process ng PER mula sa pagsumite ng kumpletong documents sa OMS?

choices.A: 20 working days
choices.B: 15 working days
choices.C: 30 working days
choices.D: 10 working days

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 5.1.10, ang application process ay dapat matapos sa loob ng 20 working days mula sa submission ng complete documents sa OMS.

level1.question: Alin sa mga sumusunod ang HINDI kabilang sa documentary requirements para sa PER application ayon sa Sec. 5.1.2?

choices.A: Manufacturing flowchart
choices.B: Certificate of Origin
choices.C: Cost of Production analysis per product
choices.D: List of raw materials

level1.reason: Hindi kasama ang Certificate of Origin sa listahan ng documentary requirements sa Sec. 5.1.2; ito ay inaaplayan pagkatapos ma-approve ang PER, ayon sa Sec. 5.1.9.

level1.question: Sino ang nagsusumite ng findings at rekomendasyon sa Approver matapos ma-evaluate ang goods?

choices.A: Exporter
choices.B: Chief of ECD
choices.C: Evaluator
choices.D: DTI-EMB

level1.reason: Sec. 5.1.7 ay nagsasaad na pagkatapos ma-evaluate ang goods, ang Evaluator ang magsusumite ng findings at recommendations sa Approver.

level1.question: Kailan maaaring magsagawa ng plant visit ayon sa Sec. 5.1.6?

choices.A: Palagi, para sa bawat application
choices.B: Kapag humiling ang exporter nito
choices.C: Kapag lumampas na sa 20 working days ang processing
choices.D: Kapag may duda sa veracity ng documents o may hindi naresolbang errors

level1.reason: Sec. 5.1.6 (a) at (b) ay nagsasaad na puwedeng magsagawa ng plant visit kapag may doubts sa veracity ng documents o may errors na hindi naayos ng applicant.

level1.question: Tuwing kailan nagbibigay ang BOC ng report sa DTI-EMB tungkol sa mga pagkakaiba ng OMS preliminary determination at final evaluation?

choices.A: Tuwing ikalimang araw ng sumusunod na buwan
choices.B: Tuwing unang araw ng buwan
choices.C: Tuwing katapusan ng taon
choices.D: Tuwing ika-15 ng bawat buwan

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 6.3, tuwing ikalimang araw ng sumusunod na buwan, magbibigay ang BOC sa DTI-EMB ng report ng mga application na may pagkakaiba.

level1.question: Ano ang mangyayari kung piliin ng Exporter na huwag gumamit ng OMS?

choices.A: Hindi na puwedeng mag-apply ng PER
choices.B: Puwede pa ring mag-submit ng application nang manual ayon sa umiiral na procedures
choices.C: Kailangan munang maghintay ng isang taon bago makapag-apply
choices.D: Awtomatikong made-deny ang application

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 7, may option ang Exporter na mag-submit ng application nang manual sa ilalim ng umiiral na procedures.

level2.question: Greenfield Exports Inc. files its PER application for a shipment leaving through Clark International Airport, which is not Port of Manila, MICP, or NAIA. Under the CMO, which office shall process and approve this application?

choices.A: The concerned Export Division of that Collection District
choices.B: The Export Coordination Division (ECD)
choices.C: The DTI-EMB
choices.D: The MISTG

level2.reason: Under Sec. 4.2.1, ECD processes applications only for POM, MICP, and NAIA; for other Collection Districts, the concerned Export Division processes and approves the application. Since Clark is not among the three named ports, the Export Division handles it.

level2.question: Exporter Dagupan Fish Products submitted its initial PER application on October 1, 2026, but the Evaluator found that the manufacturing flowchart was missing. The complete set of documents, including the flowchart, was only submitted on October 10, 2026. From which date shall the 20 working-day processing period begin to run?

choices.A: October 1, 2026, the date of the initial submission
choices.B: The date the Evaluator first reviewed the application
choices.C: The date the Approver received the Evaluator's recommendation
choices.D: October 10, 2026, the date the complete documents were submitted

level2.reason: Sec. 5.1.10 states that the 20 working-day period runs from the submission of complete documents in the OMS, not from an initial or incomplete submission. Since the flowchart completed the set only on October 10, 2026, the period begins then.

level2.question: Bohol Craft Exports uses coconut shells imported from Indonesia as a raw material for its export products. Which document must the company submit to support the origin of this particular raw material?

choices.A: Manufacturer's declaration for local raw materials
choices.B: Copy of import documents, invoice, and proof of origin for the imported raw material
choices.C: Cost of Production analysis per product
choices.D: Company profile

level2.reason: Sec. 5.1.2(e) requires a copy of import documents, invoice, and proof of origin specifically for imported raw materials, while the manufacturer's declaration under Sec. 5.1.2(g) applies only to local raw materials.

level2.question: During evaluation, the Evaluator for Sunrise Garments' PER application noticed that the submitted cost of production analysis appeared inconsistent with the company's sales invoice, raising doubts about its accuracy. Sunrise Garments was unable to clarify or correct the discrepancy. What may the Bureau do under the CMO?

choices.A: Automatically deny the PER application without further review
choices.B: Forward the application directly to DTI-EMB for resolution
choices.C: Conduct a plant visit to verify the matter
choices.D: Require the exporter to switch to a different FTA application

level2.reason: Sec. 5.1.6(b) allows a plant visit to be conducted when there are errors and inaccuracies in the submission that are not addressed by the applicant.

level2.question: After evaluation, the Approver determined that Luzon Textiles' product does not qualify as an originating good under the ASEAN-China Free Trade Agreement (ACFTA), the agreement the company applied for, but could potentially qualify under a different Agreement. What must the issued PER contain in this situation?

choices.A: The basis for disapproval and, if applicable, a recommendation of the most fitting Agreement
choices.B: Only a blank denial notice with no further explanation
choices.C: An automatic re-evaluation under all other FTAs listed in Sec. 1
choices.D: A referral letter instructing the exporter to appeal to the DTI-EMB

level2.reason: Sec. 5.1.8 provides that if the goods do not qualify as originating goods, the PER shall contain the basis for disapproval and shall recommend the most fitting Agreement, if applicable.

level2.question: In Cavite Export Corp.'s PER application, the assigned Evaluator has completed the assessment of the submitted documents and wants to move the application forward. What is the Evaluator required to do next under the CMO?

choices.A: Directly issue the PER to the exporter
choices.B: Notify the DTI-EMB for final confirmation
choices.C: Forward the application to the MISTG for system validation
choices.D: Submit the findings and recommendation to the Approver

level2.reason: Sec. 5.1.7 requires the Evaluator to submit its findings and recommendations to the Approver once the goods have been evaluated; the Evaluator does not issue the PER directly.

level2.question: Quezon Agri-Exports applied for and received its PER manually through the ECD rather than through the OMS, since it opted not to use the online system. The company later asks whether this manually obtained PER is less valid than one issued through the OMS. Based on the CMO, what is the correct answer?

choices.A: The manual PER is only provisional and must be reconfirmed online
choices.B: The manual PER has the same validity as a PER issued through the OMS
choices.C: The manual PER is valid only for GSP applications, not FTAs
choices.D: The manual PER expires after 20 working days unlike the OMS-issued PER

level2.reason: Sec. 5.1.9 states that the PER issued by the OMS will have the same validity as the PER manually applied through the ECD or equivalent office.

level2.question: Davao Fruit Exports received notification through its registered email that its PER application has been approved. The company wants to proceed with exporting its goods under preferential tariff treatment. What should Davao Fruit Exports do next under the CMO?

choices.A: Immediately ship the goods without further documentation since the PER is final proof of origin
choices.B: Wait for a second evaluation from the DTI-EMB before proceeding
choices.C: Proceed with the application for issuance of a Certificate of Origin
choices.D: Resubmit the same documents to request a Product Specific Rule

level2.reason: Sec. 5.1.9 provides that once notified of PER approval, the Exporter or authorized representative can proceed with the application for issuance of a Certificate of Origin.

level2.question: A newly-formed export company, Pampanga AgriTrade, wants to submit its first PER application through the OMS. Before it can access the Portal to submit any application, what must the company first do?

choices.A: Create an account in the OMS
choices.B: Secure prior written approval from the DTI-EMB
choices.C: Request a username and password directly from the Bureau's MISTG
choices.D: Complete a plant visit with the ECD

level2.reason: Sec. 4.2.2 requires the Exporter to first create an account in the OMS before it can access the Portal.

level2.question: Iloilo Seafood Exports authorized its customs broker to register and file PER applications on its behalf through the OMS, choosing the subscription type for an authorized representative. Whose TIN and email address should be entered in the required data fields during registration?

choices.A: The customs broker's own TIN and email address
choices.B: A generic TIN assigned by the OMS for representative accounts
choices.C: The TIN and email address of the Bureau's Account Management Office
choices.D: The TIN and email address of Iloilo Seafood Exports, the Exporter

level2.reason: Sec. 4.2.5 states that for an authorized representative, the TIN and email address of the Exporter, not the representative, shall be accomplished.

level1.question: Anong uri ng goods declaration ang sakop ng ePay para sa koleksyon ng duties at taxes, ayon sa Sec. 1?

choices.A: Lahat ng consumption entries na isinampa gamit ang E2M System
choices.B: Additional assessments na galing sa Post Entry Modification
choices.C: Goods declaration na manually processed sa informal entry procedure
choices.D: Mga entry na binayaran na sa cashier ng Port ng Bureau

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 1, sakop ng Order ang koleksyon ng duties at taxes sa goods na covered ng goods declaration na manually processed sa ilalim ng informal entry procedure, pati ang miscellaneous fees na bayad sa Bureau gamit ang ePay. Ang E2M consumption entries at Post Entry Modification assessments ay excluded (Sec. 6).

level1.question: Ayon sa Sec. 2.2, kailan available ang online payment channels na naka-integrate sa ePay?

choices.A: Sa 24/7 na basehan
choices.B: Tuwing working days lamang ng Bureau
choices.C: Hanggang cut-off time ng Collection Division ng Port
choices.D: Tuwing weekdays mula 8:00 AM hanggang 5:00 PM

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 2.2, layunin ng Order na magbigay ng user interface bilang alternative mode of payment sa duties, taxes, at miscellaneous fees, na naka-integrate sa iba't ibang online payment channels na available sa 24/7 basis.

level1.question: Ano ang Order of Payment (OP) ayon sa Sec. 3.2?

choices.A: Resibo na inilalabas ng cashier ng Port matapos magbayad ang stakeholder
choices.B: Report ng daily collection na isinusumite ng Collection Division sa STAD at RAD
choices.C: Account Creation Form na isinusumite ng BOC personnel na mag-iisyu ng OP
choices.D: Instruksyon sa ePay para magbayad ang external stakeholder ng duties, taxes, o miscellaneous fees

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 3.2, ang Order of Payment ay ang mga instruksyon na ibinibigay sa pamamagitan ng ePay para sa external stakeholder upang bayaran ang duties, taxes, at/o miscellaneous fees na due sa Bureau.

level1.question: Ano ang Fixed Values ayon sa Sec. 3.5?

choices.A: Halaga ng duties at taxes na kinukuwenta sa bawat assessment ng goods na ini-import
choices.B: Fixed na halaga ng administrative o miscellaneous fees sa ilalim ng umiiral na rules
choices.C: Halagang inilalagay ng BOC personnel sa bawat OP ayon sa kanyang sariling pagpapasya
choices.D: Halaga ng bayad na itinatakda ng Digital Payment Provider sa bawat payment channel

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 3.5, ang Fixed Values ay ang fixed amount ng administrative fees o miscellaneous fees na itinakda ng existing rules and regulations, tulad ng Customs Documentary Stamp, Document Stamp Tax, Registration Charge for Auction, Registration Charge for Account Management Office, at Accreditation Charge.

level1.question: Ano ang tawag sa accredited juridical entities na nagbibigay ng digital payment platforms para sa online payment ng external stakeholders, ayon sa Sec. 3.4?

choices.A: Digital Payment Platform
choices.B: Electronic Payment Portal System
choices.C: Digital Payment Provider
choices.D: Order of Payment

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 3.4, ang Digital Payment Provider ay ang accredited juridical entities na nagbibigay ng digital payment platforms. Ang Digital Payment Platform (Sec. 3.3) naman ay ang ICT-enabled mechanism na nag-uugnay sa ePay ng BOC at financial institutions.

level1.question: Aling opisina ang nagma-maintain ng ePay ayon sa Sec. 4.1?

choices.A: MISTG
choices.B: RAD
choices.C: STAD
choices.D: Collection Division

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 4.1, ang ePay ay imi-maintain ng Management Information System and Technology Group (MISTG).

level1.question: Kanino isinusumite ang Account Creation Form (Annex A) at indorsement letter ng chief concerned para sa account ng BOC personnel na mag-iisyu ng OP, ayon sa Sec. 4.2?

choices.A: RAD
choices.B: STAD
choices.C: Collection Division ng Port
choices.D: TSD ng MISTG

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 4.2, ang request para sa account creation ay isinusumite sa Technical Support Division (TSD) ng MISTG sa pamamagitan ng pagkumpleto ng Account Creation Form (Annex A) kasama ang indorsement letter mula sa chief concerned, electronically sa pamamagitan ng email.

level1.question: Saan ipinapadala ang login authentication code ng ePay user, ayon sa Sec. 4.5?

choices.A: Sa personal email address na ibinigay ng user sa BOC
choices.B: Sa BOC official email ng user (<name>@customs.gov.ph)
choices.C: Sa mobile number na naka-register sa account ng user
choices.D: Sa email ng chief concerned na nag-indorse ng account

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 4.5, para sa security at accountability, ang login authentication code ay ipapadala sa email ng user na gumagamit ng BOC official domain, at tanging authorized personnel na gumagamit ng BOC official domain ang bibigyan ng access sa system.

level1.question: Aling opisina ang nagre-reconcile ng daily ePay collection report laban sa collection report ng Digital Payment Provider, ayon sa Sec. 4.8?

choices.A: STAD
choices.B: Collection Division ng Port
choices.C: RAD
choices.D: MISTG

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 4.8, ang Revenue Accounting Division (RAD) ang nagre-reconcile ng daily ePay collection report laban sa submitted collection report ng Digital Payment Provider. Ang Collection Division ng Ports ay nagsusumite ng daily/monthly collection report sa STAD at RAD.

level1.question: Alin sa mga sumusunod ang mga opisinang responsable sa pag-generate ng reports mula sa data na nakalap sa ePay, ayon sa Sec. 4.7?

choices.A: MISTG lamang, dahil ito ang nagma-maintain ng ePay at nag-iipon ng data
choices.B: Collection Division ng Port, RAD, STAD, at iba pang concerned offices
choices.C: Collection Division ng Port at TSD lamang, bilang mga direktang gumagamit ng system
choices.D: RAD at MISTG lamang, dahil sila ang tumatanggap ng collection reports

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 4.7, ang Collection Division ng Port, RAD, STAD, at iba pang concerned offices ang responsable sa pag-generate ng reports mula sa data na nakalap sa ePay.

level2.question: A port's Collection Division is reviewing two transactions. Shipment 1 is covered by a goods declaration manually processed under the informal entry procedure. Shipment 2 is a consumption entry filed through the Bureau's E2M System that later received an additional assessment through Post Entry Modification. For which transaction(s) may the duties and taxes be collected through ePay under this Order?

choices.A: Both shipments
choices.B: Shipment 1 only
choices.C: Shipment 2 only
choices.D: Neither shipment

level2.reason: Under Sec. 1, the Order covers duties and taxes on goods covered by a goods declaration manually processed under the informal entry procedure. Under Sec. 6, all consumption entries filed using the E2M System, including additional assessments from Post Entry Modification, are excluded. Only Shipment 1 is covered.

level2.question: Greenline Trading generated an Order of Payment for miscellaneous fees but did not pay it within its validity period. When it later tries to pay, the ePay shows the OP as expired. What must Greenline do?

choices.A: Pay the same OP through the cashier after printing it again
choices.B: Reuse the same OP Reference Number with a revised remarks entry
choices.C: Apply for a new OP
choices.D: Ask the MISTG to reactivate the expired OP

level2.reason: Under Secs. 5.1.7 and 5.2.9, OPs that remain unpaid after their validity are tagged as 'Expired' in the ePay, and the external stakeholder can no longer use the expired OP for payment and must instead apply for a new OP.

level2.question: Two stakeholders need to pay Fixed Values through ePay. Ramon generated his own OP using the stakeholder procedure and is on the Order of Payment page, having not yet clicked Proceed to Payment. Sofia's OP was generated for her by a concerned BOC office, and she is on the Order of Payment page. Who may still add or delete miscellaneous items?

choices.A: Ramon only
choices.B: Sofia only
choices.C: Both of them
choices.D: Neither of them

level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.1.9, a stakeholder who generated his own OP can still add or delete miscellaneous items on the Order of Payment page, until he clicks Proceed to Payment (Sec. 5.1.11). Under Sec. 5.2.12, when the OP was generated by a concerned BOC office, the stakeholder can no longer add or delete items. Only Ramon may still do so.

level2.question: A stakeholder with an unexpired OP chooses 'Pay Via ePay' and wants to pay using an e-wallet. Which sequence is correct under Sec. 5?

choices.A: Print the OP, bring it to the cashier, and select the e-wallet channel at the cashier window
choices.B: Select the e-wallet channel on the ePay homepage before any OP Reference Number is generated
choices.C: Select the e-wallet channel, then wait for the BOC office to confirm the payment on his behalf
choices.D: Select a Digital Payment Provider, pick the e-wallet on its page, enter the details, and confirm payment

level2.reason: Under Secs. 5.1.12 to 5.1.14 (and 5.2.14 to 5.2.16), after choosing 'Pay Via ePay' the stakeholder chooses the Digital Payment Provider, is redirected to the provider's page to choose the payment channel (such as e-Wallet), provides the information required by that channel, and confirms payment. Printing the OP for the cashier applies only to 'Pay Via Cashier'.

level2.question: A stakeholder tells a port's Collection Division that he paid, through an e-wallet, an OP that the Division issued. Who must validate the payment, and how?

choices.A: The Digital Payment Provider, by emailing the Division the stakeholder's receipt
choices.B: The BOC office that issued the OP, by checking its payment status in ePay
choices.C: The stakeholder, by presenting his e-wallet receipt to the MISTG
choices.D: The RAD, by reconciling the Digital Payment Provider's monthly report

level2.reason: Under Sec. 7 (and Sec. 4.6), it is the responsibility of the concerned BOC office or unit that issued the OP to validate payment by checking the payment status of the generated OP, where OPs with payments made are reflected as tagged in the ePay.

level2.question: A BOC officer issued an OP for a stakeholder's miscellaneous fees but never checked the OP's payment status. What is the consequence under the Order?

choices.A: No consequence, as the ePay confirms all payments for the office automatically
choices.B: Automatic removal from the post without administrative proceedings
choices.C: A ground for administrative sanctions under Civil Service law and regulations
choices.D: A fine equal to the total amount stated in the unconfirmed OP

level2.reason: Under Sec. 7, the BOC office that issued the OP must validate payment. Under Sec. 8, failure to confirm payment is a ground for administrative sanctions under existing Civil Service law, rules and regulations, without prejudice to other criminal or civil liability under applicable law.

level2.question: Carlo, a BOC personnel authorized to issue OPs, asks that his ePay login authentication code be sent to his personal email address because it is easier to access. Can this be done under the Order?

choices.A: No, because it is sent to the user's BOC official domain email
choices.B: Yes, if the chief concerned approves the request in writing
choices.C: Yes, if he uses the BOC email address for monitoring only
choices.D: No, because the code is sent only to the user's mobile number

level2.reason: Under Sec. 4.5, a login authentication code is sent to the email of the user using the BOC official domain (<name>@customs.gov.ph), and only authorized personnel using the BOC official domain are granted access to the system. Nothing in the Order allows a personal email address.

level2.question: A BOC office is generating an OP for a stakeholder under Sec. 5.2 for two miscellaneous items: the Customs Documentary Stamp, which is a Fixed Value, and an item that is Not Fixed. How should the user enter them?

choices.A: Tick the checkbox for both items without entering any amount at all
choices.B: Enter an amount for both items, then click Add for each of them
choices.C: Enter an amount for the Fixed item and tick only the Not Fixed item
choices.D: Tick the box for the Fixed item; enter an amount for the Not Fixed item

level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.2.6, if the miscellaneous item is Not Fixed (NF), the user enters the amount and clicks Add; if it is Fixed (F), the user just ticks the checkbox and clicks Add. Under Sec. 3.5, the Customs Documentary Stamp is a Fixed Value.

level2.question: Mario, a stakeholder, wants to pay Fixed Values through ePay and generates his own OP. He clicks the 'Generate Order of Payment' button, enters the Consignee/Company and his Email Address, selects the Port, and clicks Request. What happens next?

choices.A: He receives a link at the email address entered, redirecting him to ePay.
choices.B: He immediately receives the OP Reference Number and validity period by email.
choices.C: The Order of Payment page appears, where he chooses Pay Via Cashier or Pay Via ePay.
choices.D: A concerned BOC office must first generate the OP on his behalf.

level2.reason: Under Secs. 5.1.1 to 5.1.3, after the stakeholder clicks Request, he receives a link through the email address entered and is redirected to the BOC ePay by clicking it. The OP Reference Number and validity period are emailed only later (Sec. 5.1.7), after the miscellaneous items are saved.

level2.question: A Port Collector asks which office is authorized to issue the memorandum setting the schedule for the nationwide implementation of ePay. Who is authorized under the Order?

choices.A: RAD, through a memorandum
choices.B: STAD, through a memorandum
choices.C: MISTG, through a memorandum
choices.D: The Collection Division of the Ports, through a memorandum

level2.reason: Under Sec. 9, the MISTG is authorized to issue a Memorandum on the schedule of the nationwide implementation of the ePay.

level1.question: Ayon sa Sec. 4.1, aling Proof of Origin ang tatanggapin lang ng Bureau sa effectivity ng Order na ito?

choices.A: OD na ginawa ng kahit anong exporter o producer
choices.B: CO Form PH-KR lamang, hindi kasama ang OD
choices.C: OD ng Approved Exporter lamang, hindi kasama ang CO
choices.D: CO Form PH-KR at OD na inisyu ng Approved Exporter

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 4.1, CO Form PH-KR at Origin Declaration (OD) na inisyu ng Approved Exporter lang ang tatanggapin ng Bureau sa effectivity ng Order. Ang OD ng exporter o producer ay ipapatupad nang hindi lalampas sa sampung (10) taon pagkatapos ng date of entry into force ng Agreement.

level1.question: Aling unit ng Bureau ang nag-e-evaluate ng authenticity, accuracy, at validity ng Proof of Origin na isinumite ng importers at nagbibigay ng PH-KR FTA preferential tariff rates, ayon sa Sec. 3.10?

choices.A: Export Coordination Division (ECD)
choices.B: Preferential Rate Unit (PRU) o ang equivalent unit nito sa ports
choices.C: Customer Care Center (CCC)
choices.D: Export Division ng port

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 3.10 (at Sec. 4.6), ang Preferential Rate Unit (PRU) o ang equivalent unit nito sa lahat ng ports ang nag-e-evaluate ng authenticity, accuracy, at validity ng Proof of Origin ng importers at nagbibigay ng PH-KR FTA preferential tariff rates. Ang ECD naman ay nagpoproseso ng Approved Exporter applications at nagve-verify ng originating status (Sec. 3.4).

level1.question: Ayon sa Secs. 4.1 at 5.2.2, hanggang kailan dapat ipatupad ang Origin Declaration na ginawa ng exporter o producer?

choices.A: Hindi lalampas sa sampung (10) taon pagkatapos ng date of entry into force ng Agreement
choices.B: Hindi lalampas sa limang (5) taon pagkatapos ng date of entry into force ng Agreement
choices.C: Hindi lalampas sa tatlong (3) taon pagkatapos ng date of entry into force ng Agreement
choices.D: Hindi lalampas sa labinlimang (15) taon pagkatapos ng date of entry into force ng Agreement

level1.reason: Sa Secs. 4.1 at 5.2.2, ang Origin Declaration ng exporter o producer ay ipapatupad nang hindi lalampas sa sampung (10) taon pagkatapos ng date of entry into force ng PH-KR FTA.

level1.question: Ayon sa Sec. 4.2, ano ang dapat ibigay ng bawat Party sa PH-KR FTA sa pamamagitan ng contact points?

choices.A: Listahan ng lahat ng Approved Exporters at kanilang authorization codes
choices.B: Listahan ng goods na may preferential tariff rate sa ilalim ng Agreement
choices.C: Listahan ng pangalan, address, specimen signatures, at specimen ng official seals ng issuing body nito
choices.D: Listahan ng importers na nag-claim ng preferential tariff treatment

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 4.2, bawat Party ay magbibigay, sa hard copy o soft copy, ng listahan ng mga pangalan, address, specimen signatures, at specimen ng official seals ng issuing body nito sa pamamagitan ng contact points. Ang anumang pagbabago ay dapat agad ding ibigay sa parehong paraan.

level1.question: Sa PER application sa ilalim ng Sec. 5.1.1(a), kanino dapat naka-address ang request letter na nagsasabi ng intensyong gamitin ang PH-KR FTA?

choices.A: AOCG Deputy Commissioner
choices.B: ECD Chief
choices.C: District Collector ng port
choices.D: Chief ng Customer Care Center

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 5.1.1(a), ang request letter ay naka-address sa ECD Chief at nagsasaad ng intensyong gamitin ang PH-KR FTA, description ng goods, at kaukulang HS Codes.

level1.question: Ano ang puwedeng gawin ng Approved Exporter ayon sa Sec. 5.5.3?

level1.question: Ayon sa Sec. 6.1, ano ang unang hakbang sa pagkakasunod-sunod ng verification na maaaring gawin ng customs authority ng importing Party?

choices.D: Written request sa issuing authority ng exporting Party

Kaya ang unang hakbang ay written request sa importer.

level2.question: Luzon Export Corp. is an Approved Exporter. At the time of exportation, it cannot complete the Origin Declaration (OD) on the commercial invoice. On which other documents may it complete the OD under Sec. 5.6.1?

choices.B: A billing statement or a packing list

choices.D: The Certificate of Registration or the written authorization

level2.reason: Under the last paragraph of Sec. 5.6.1, the OD of an Approved Exporter is completed on the commercial invoice, but if it cannot be completed on the commercial invoice at the time of exportation, it may be completed on either a billing statement or a packing list.

level2.question: Kaya Textiles Inc. applies for Approved Exporter status. It has sound bookkeeping and record keeping, good compliance under the Bureau's risk management, an authorized signatory competent in ROO application, and willingness to undergo regular monitoring and inspection. However, it started transacting with the Bureau only 10 months before the date of its application. Which action by the ECD is correct under Secs. 5.4.3 and 5.4.4?

choices.A: Grant the status, since four of the five criteria have been satisfied by Kaya

choices.D: Issue a letter of disapproval because it has transacted for less than one year

level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.4.3(a), the exporter must have been transacting with the Bureau at least one (1) year prior to the date of application. level2.question: Island Traders Inc. is a trader that wants to become an Approved Exporter for goods made by an independent producer. choices.B: A cost of production analysis for each product of the independent producer
choices.C: A manufacturing flowchart showing the production process of the producer
choices.D: A copy of the sales invoice for the local raw materials of the producer

level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.4.1(d), in the case of a trader, the application must include a producer's declaration indicating the originating status of the good for which it will complete an OD and the readiness of the producer to cooperate in verification procedures. The other documents are not listed in Sec. 5.4.1.

level2.question: Manila Foods Inc. applies for a CO Form PH-KR. It has the Export Declaration, Commercial Invoice, Bill of Lading, and an approved PER, and its goods require no other permits. Which required document is still missing under Sec. 5.3.1?

choices.A: Company profile

choices.D: Producer's declaration

level2.question: Visayas Marine Products applied for a CO Form PH-KR at the Export Division of a port outside Metro Manila, and the application was approved. What happens to the signed CO under Sec. 5.3.3?

choices.A: It is sent directly by the Export Division to the customs authority of the importing Party.
choices.B: It is transmitted back to the CCC, where the exporter and importer copies are retrieved.

choices.D: It is kept by the ECD until the importer formally requests a copy of it.

level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.3.3, upon approval the Export Division affixes the signature of the authorized signatory and the BOC seal, and the signed CO with its unique CO reference number is transmitted back to the CCC for retrieval of the copies intended for the exporter and importer.

level2.question: The Philippine customs authority, as importing Party, is verifying the origin of goods under the PH-KR FTA. It has already sent a written request for additional information to the importer. Under Sec. 6.1, what is the next step in the order of verification?

choices.A: A verification visit to the premises of the exporter or producer
choices.B: A written request to the issuing authority of the exporting Party
choices.C: A written request for information from the exporter or producer
choices.D: A second written request for information to the importer

level2.reason: Under Sec. 6.1, verification may be conducted in this order: (a) written requests to the importer, (b) written requests to the exporter or producer, (c) written requests to the issuing authority of the exporting Party, and (d) verification visits. After step (a), the next step is (b).

level2.question: A PRU at the Port of Cebu has reasonable doubt about the accuracy of the origin information in a Proof of Origin presented by an importer. What should the PRU do under the Order?

choices.A: Request verification through the ECD
choices.B: Deny the claim immediately without any verification
choices.C: Ask the CCC to contact the exporter abroad
choices.D: Send its own verification team to the exporter's premises

Under Sec. 4.9, the ECD carries out the verification, by documents requested from the exporter or producer or by a verification visit.

level2.question: An employee of Harbor Spices Corp., an Approved Exporter, used the company's authorization code to complete an OD for goods that did not qualify as originating. Under Sec. 5.5.1, who bears responsibility for the misuse?

choices.D: Harbor Spices Corp., which accepts full responsibility for all ODs it completes

level2.question: Bagong Tela Inc., a producer in Cebu, wants its goods evaluated before exportation so it can claim PH-KR FTA preferential tariff treatment. Which procedure is correct under Secs. 5.1.1 and 5.1.2?

choices.A: Apply to the ECD, upload the documents through the Bureau's Portal, and then submit hard copies to the CCC.

Under Sec. 5.1.2, the application is submitted through the Bureau's Portal with all documents uploaded, and hard copies are also submitted to the CCC.

level2.question: Prime Coco Exports, an Approved Exporter, completes an OD in its own format. It includes the exporter's, producer's, and importer's names and addresses, the description and six-digit HS Code, the authorization code, a unique reference number, the origin conferring criterion, the certification by an authorized signatory, the quantity, the certifier's name and signature, and the completion date. It uses a criterion other than Regional Value Content, and the OD is written in Filipino. Does the OD comply with Sec. 5.6.1?

choices.A: Yes, because Approved Exporters can use any format
choices.B: No, because the OD must follow Annex A exactly
choices.C: No, because the OD must be in the English language
choices.D: No, because the OD must bear the BOC seal

level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.6.1, an Approved Exporter may use any format for the OD provided it contains the required information, is in the English language, bears the name and signature of the certifying person, and bears the completion date. All required information is present (the FOB value is needed only if the Regional Value Content criterion is used), but the OD is in Filipino, so it fails Sec. 5.6.1(b).

level1.question: Ayon sa Sec. 3.13, ano ang tinatawag na Proof of Origin sa ilalim ng Order na ito?

choices.A: Product Evaluation Report na inisyu ng ECD o Export Division/Unit

choices.C: Authorization Code na ibinigay sa Approved Exporter
choices.D: Listahan ng raw materials na ginamit sa production ng export goods

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 3.13, ang Proof of Origin ay either isang Certificate of Origin (CO) na inisyu ng issuing body o isang Declaration of Origin (DO) ng Approved Exporter. Ang PER (Sec. 3.11) ay hiwalay na dokumento na resulta ng evaluation ng export products.

level1.question: Aling division sa ilalim ng AOCG ng BOC ang nagpoproseso ng applications ng Approved Exporters at nagsasagawa ng verification ng originating status ng goods, ayon sa Sec. 3.5?

choices.D: Cash Division

Ang PRU naman ay nag-e-evaluate ng Proof of Origin ng importers (Sec. 3.12).

level1.question: Ano ang Tariff Differential ayon sa Sec. 3.16?

choices.A: Ibang tariff treatment na inaaplay ng RCEP importing Party sa iba't ibang RCEP Parties para sa parehong RCEP originating good
choices.B: Pagkakaiba ng MFN rate at RCEP rate na inaaplay ng importing Party sa iisang originating good

choices.D: Excess duties at taxes na binayaran ng importer dahil hindi nabigyan ng preferential tariff treatment

level1.question: Ayon sa Sec. 4.2, aling Proof of Origin ang tatanggapin ng BOC sa effectivity ng Order na ito?

choices.A: DO na inisyu ng kahit anong exporter o producer
choices.B: Back-to-back Proof of Origin na hindi batay sa CO o DO ng Approved Exporter
choices.C: CO Form RCEP lamang, hindi kasama ang DO

Ang DO ng exporter o producer ay tatanggapin lang kapag na-implement na ng Pilipinas ang subparagraph 1(c), Article 3.16 ng RCEP Agreement, at ang back-to-back Proof of Origin ay tatanggapin lang kung batay sa CO o DO ng Approved Exporter.

level1.question: Ayon sa Sec. 4.4, ano ang puwedeng gawin ng importer na hindi nag-claim ng RCEP preferential tariff treatment sa oras ng importation?

Kailangan niyang magsumite ng Proof of Origin at iba pang ebidensya na originating good ito (Sec. 4.4.1), at ng iba pang dokumentong hihingin ng BOC (Sec. 4.4.2).

level1.question: Ayon sa Sec. 5.3.4, ilang working days ang ibinibigay sa ECD para ibigay ang Approved Exporter status sa pamamagitan ng written authorization na may authorization code, mula sa receipt ng complete application?

Kung hindi, maglalabas ito ng letter of disapproval na may dahilan ng denial.

level1.question: Ayon sa Sec. 5.3.3(a), gaano katagal nang dapat nakikipag-transact sa BOC ang exporter bago ang petsa ng application para maituring na legitimate exporter at maging Approved Exporter?

level1.question: Gaano katagal dapat itago ng Approved Exporter ang kopya ng DO at ng lahat ng dokumentong sumusuporta sa originating status ng good, ayon sa Sec. 5.4.2?

level1.question: Ayon sa Sec. 5.7.1(b), ano ang additional requirement para sa goods na nakalista sa Annex 1 ng Order para ang exporting Party ang maging RCEP Country of Origin?

level1.question: Saan mag-a-apply para sa Product Evaluation Report (PER) ang producer o trader na nasa labas ng Metro Manila, ayon sa Sec. 5.1.1?

choices.A: Export Division/Unit
choices.B: ECD
choices.C: AOCG Deputy Commissioner
choices.D: PRU

level2.question: Rizal Foods Inc., a producer in Metro Manila, applies for a Product Evaluation Report (PER) to claim RCEP preferential tariff treatment, and the ECD receives its complete documents. The ECD determines that a plant visit is necessary and conducts one. Assuming the ECD uses the full time allowed by the Order, within how many working days from receipt of the complete documents must it act on the application?

choices.A: 21 working days
choices.B: 31 working days
choices.C: 35 working days
choices.D: 45 working days

level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.1.3, the ECD or Export Division/Unit must act on the PER application within twenty-one (21) working days from receipt of complete documents, and the evaluation may be extended for another ten (10) working days in case of plant visits. Because a plant visit was conducted, the total is 21 + 10 = 31 working days.

level2.question: Mabuhay Exports Corp. applies for Approved Exporter status. It has transacted with the BOC for 18 months, has sound bookkeeping and record keeping, has good compliance under BOC risk management, has a signatory competent in ROO application, and agrees to regular monitoring and inspection. However, its first shipment to an RCEP Party was made only 8 months ago. Is its application meritorious under Sec. 5.3.3?

choices.A: Yes, because it has transacted with the BOC for at least one year
choices.B: Yes, because its compliance and record keeping are sound
choices.C: No, because it has transacted with the BOC for less than two years
choices.D: No, because it has exported to an RCEP Party for less than one year

level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.3.3(b), the exporter must have been exporting products to at least one RCEP Party for at least one (1) year. Mabuhay has exported to an RCEP Party for only 8 months, so it fails this criterion even though it satisfies the others, including the one-year BOC transaction requirement in Sec. 5.3.3(a). Under Sec. 5.3.4, the ECD would then issue a letter of disapproval stating the reasons.

level2.question: Pacific Trading Corp., a Philippine Approved Exporter, holds a valid original CO covering 1,000 cartons of goods. The original CO is valid until 30 September 2023. It will re-export 400 cartons in a partial shipment, with no processing other than repacking, and will complete a back-to-back DO. Which back-to-back DO complies with Sec. 5.6.1?

choices.A: Valid until 31 October 2023 and showing 400 cartons
choices.B: Valid until 30 September 2023 and showing 1,000 cartons
choices.C: Valid until 30 September 2023 and showing 400 cartons
choices.D: Valid until 30 September 2023 and showing 1,200 cartons

Under Sec. 5.6.1(e), for partial export shipments the partial export quantity is shown instead of the full quantity, and the total re-exported may not exceed the original total. The compliant DO therefore shows 400 cartons.

level2.question: Under EO No. 25, the Philippines applies different RCEP rates to the same originating good from different RCEP Parties: 3% for Party W, 5% for Party X, 8% for Party Y, and 10% for Party Z. A good was produced in Party X using originating materials from Party X and Party Y, while Parties W and Z contributed none. The importer chooses to claim under Sec. 5.8.3(a). What is the highest rate at which it may claim?
level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.8.3(a), the importer may claim at the highest rate of customs duty the importing Party applies to the same originating good from any of the RCEP Parties contributing originating materials used in its production. The contributing Parties are X (5%) and Y (8%), so the highest is 8%. The 10% rate would only be available under Sec. 5.8.3(b), which is a different option, and the importer did not choose it.

level2.question: A Preferential Rate Unit (PRU) at a port has reasonable doubt about the authenticity of a CO submitted by an importer and decides to pursue a verification through a written request. How should the written request be processed under Sec. 6.1?

choices.A: The PRU sends it directly to the issuing body of the RCEP exporting Party.
choices.B: The PRU endorses it through the District Collector, and it is forwarded to the AOCG through the ECD.
choices.C: The PRU forwards it to the CCC, which sends it to the exporter.
choices.D: The District Collector sends it to the AOCG Deputy Commissioner, who sends it to the importer.

Under Sec. 6.1.5, the ECD then sends the request to the importer, exporter, producer, or issuing body or competent authority. The PRU may request verification through the ECD when it has reasonable doubt (Sec. 4.9).

level2.question: Goods imported under a claim for RCEP preferential tariff treatment have not yet been released, and the PRU has requested verification of the Proof of Origin covering all the goods in the shipment. The duties and taxes would be Php 480,000.00 at the MFN rate and Php 310,000.00 at the RCEP rate. What guarantee is required before release?

choices.D: Manager's check for Php 480,000.00

Php 480,000.00 - Php 310,000.00 = Php 170,000.00. The Cash Division holds the check in abeyance until the ECD orders its deposit or return.

level2.question: Alba Electronics Inc. imported goods and claimed RCEP preferential tariff treatment. The PRU requested a verification visit to the foreign exporter, and the exporter refused to consent within the 30 days given to it. What may the BOC do under Sec. 6.1.9?

choices.A: The BOC may deny the claim for preferential tariff treatment.
choices.B: The BOC must conduct the visit on its own within 60 days.
choices.C: The BOC must grant the claim and close the verification.
choices.D: The BOC must suspend all future imports of the importer.

level2.reason: Under Sec. 6.1.9, the exporter, producer, or competent authority has thirty (30) days from receipt of the written request to consent to or refuse the verification visit. If the visit is refused, the claim for preferential tariff treatment may be denied.

level2.question: Delta Circuits Inc. imported goods covered by a CO, and the ECD received the foreign exporter's consent to a verification visit on 10 March 2024. The ECD conducted the visit on 1 May 2024. Assume periods are counted in calendar days, starting the day after the triggering date. By what date must the ECD make its decision?

choices.A: 9 April 2024

Counting 30 days from 1 May 2024 gives 31 May 2024.

level2.question: On 2 October 2023, a written request for verification of a Proof of Origin from an RCEP importing Party, addressed to a Philippine exporter, was received by the AOCG Deputy Commissioner with a copy furnished to the ECD Chief. Under Sec. 6.2.5, the ECD must transmit the verification result to the importing Party within ninety (90) days from receipt of the written request, which is 31 December 2023.

level2.question: Greenfield Spices Corp. is an Approved Exporter authorized by the BOC only for dried mango products. It also has complete documents proving that its dried pineapple chips meet the RCEP origin requirements. It completes a DO for a shipment of dried pineapple chips. Is this allowed under the Order?

choices.C: Yes, if it informs the BOC of the change within the next three years
choices.D: No, because DOs may be completed only after the PRU verifies the goods

Having the documents is not enough; the pineapple chips are not covered by its authorization, so the DO is not allowed.

level1.question: Ayon sa Sec. 3.1.1, hanggang ilang porsyento ng duty na ipinataw ng batas ang maaaring i-claim bilang Duty Drawback para sa imported fuel na ginamit sa propulsion ng sea vessel na engaged sa international trade?

choices.A: Hanggang 50%
choices.B: Hanggang 99%

choices.D: Hanggang 90%

level2.question: Kalinaw Ventures Corp. is preparing a Duty Drawback claim with a total claim amount of Php 1,350,000.00 and has already gathered complete documents. level2.question: Dalisay Foods Corp. will file a Duty Drawback claim under Sec. 3.1.3 for goods that were exported on 5 February 2024. On 1 July 2024, which is 35 days before the six-month filing period lapses, it requests an extension to file. Assume each period ends on the same calendar date on which it began (for example, six months from 5 February ends on 5 August). choices.B: 1 July 2025
choices.C: 5 February 2025
choices.D: 5 August 2025

level2.reason: Under Sec. 3.5.2, a Sec. 3.1.3 claim must be filed within six months from exportation, and the claimant may request a further six months if the request is made thirty (30) days before the six-month period lapses. Here the request was made 35 days before, so it qualifies. The actual filing may not exceed one (1) year from the date of exportation, which is 5 February 2025.

level2.question: Sunrise Packaging Inc. files a Duty Drawback claim under Sec. 3.1.3 for goods that were constructive exports. The delivery receipt is dated 8 May 2024, the sales invoice is dated 2 May 2024, the import duties were paid on 10 January 2024, and the Shipment Information Sheet was attested on 30 May 2024. From which date is the start of the prescriptive period reckoned with respect to the exportation?

choices.C: 10 January 2024

level2.reason: Under Sec. 3.5.4(c), the start of the prescriptive period is reckoned from the date of delivery receipt in case of constructive exports. The date duties were paid (Sec. 3.5.4(a)) applies to importations, and the loading date (Sec. 3.5.4(b)) applies to actual exports, so the delivery receipt date of 8 May 2024 controls for the exportation.

level2.question: Luzon Plastics Inc. imported resin on 3 March 2023 and paid the duties on the same day. It used the resin to make a single type of product and exported all of it on 20 June 2024. It seeks a refund of 80% of the duties paid on the resin used, and NEDA has made no determination requiring a Certification on Non-availability of locally-produced substitutes. Which requirement under Sec. 3.1.3 does the claim fail to satisfy?

choices.A: The refund must not exceed 100% of the duties paid on the materials used
choices.B: There must be no NEDA determination requiring a Certification on Non-availability
choices.C: An equitable apportionment must be made when two or more products result
choices.D: Exportation must be made within one year after the importation of the materials

level2.reason: Under Sec. 3.1.3(d), exportation must be made within one (1) year after the importation of the materials used. The resin was imported on 3 March 2023 and the products were exported on 20 June 2024, which is more than one year later. The other conditions are met on the stated facts: 80% is within the 100% cap (Sec. 3.1.3(b)), NEDA made no determination (Sec. 3.1.3(c)), and only one product resulted (Sec. 3.1.3(e)).

level2.question: Pinoy Mills Corp. imported bulk wheat, paid the duties, and used it to produce flour that it exported. It is filing a claim under Sec. 3.1.3 and it is also the importer of the wheat. The Bunkering Permit and the Schedule of Fuel Oil Purchases are proof of exportation items for Secs. 3.1.1 and 3.1.2 claims, and the waiver certification is for cases where the importer is not the claimant, which is not the case here.

level2.question: A claimant's Duty Drawback documents are complete, and the TCC Secretariat has verified that all duties subject of the claim were paid and remitted to the Bureau of the Treasury. level2.question: Tala Garments Inc. files a Duty Drawback claim under Sec. 3.1.3. Its verified import documents show 3,000 kg of fabric with total duties paid of Php 45,000.00. The ITDI Formula of Conversion requires 2 kg of fabric per garment. Verified export documents show 1,000 garments exported, but 100 of them were exported beyond the prescriptive period and are disallowed. What amount of Duty Drawback should be computed?
level2.reason: Under Sec. 4.2.4(d), the allowable export quantity is the verified export quantity less disallowances due to prescriptive periods: 1,000 - 100 = 900 garments. Fabric used = 900 x 2 kg = 1,800 kg, which does not exceed the 3,000 kg imported. Duty per kg = Php 45,000.00 / 3,000 kg = Php 15.00. Duty Drawback = 1,800 kg x Php 15.00 = Php 27,000.00.

level2.question: Petrogen Corp., a non-electric utility, imported crude oil on which it paid the duty imposed by law of Php 2,000,000.00. level2.reason: Under Sec. 3.1.2, crude oil imported by non-electric utilities and sold to electric utilities for the generation of electric power may be refunded up to a maximum of fifty percent (50%) of the duty imposed by law. 50% x Php 2,000,000.00 = Php 1,000,000.00. The 99% limit in Sec. 3.1.1 applies to fuel used for propulsion of qualified vessels and international flights, not to this situation.

level2.question: Kestrel Parts Ltd. ships three separate packages through an AECO to the same consignee, Mario Dela Cruz. All three packages arrive in Manila on the same date, and each is valued at Php18,000 FOB. The AECO plans to file three separate informal entries, one for each package. How should the shipments be treated under CMO 09-2021?

choices.B: As three De Minimis shipments covered by the detailed CIFCM as the Goods Declaration
choices.C: As a single consignment filed under the formal entry process
choices.D: As a single Low-Value, Dutiable shipment filed under the informal entry process

level2.reason: Under Sec. 23, low-value shipments with the same shipper and the same consignee whose aggregate value is Php50,000.00 or more at the date of arrival are treated as a single consignment and filed under the formal entry process. Here, 3 x Php18,000 = Php54,000, which exceeds the threshold, so the AECO cannot file three separate informal entries.

level2.question: At the request of an AECO, a customs examiner works 4 hours of overtime on a Sunday, which is the examiner's rest day. The monthly salary of the position being designated is Php44,000. Using the formula in CMO 09-2021, how much overtime pay is the examiner entitled to?
level2.reason: Under Secs. 5.4.3 and 5.4.4, the hourly rate is Monthly Salary/22 days/8 hrs, and overtime on a rest day is the hourly rate plus 50%. Hourly rate = 44,000/22/8 = Php250; rest-day overtime rate = 250 x 1.5 = Php375; for 4 hours, 375 x 4 = Php1,500.

level2.question: An aircraft arrives in Manila at 2:00 PM with an IFCM that was submitted on time. The AECO later discovers three cartons not listed in the IFCM and submits a supplemental IFCM, in both hard copy and electronic form, at 9:30 PM on the same day. What is the status of the three cartons?

choices.B: They are accepted, but they must be covered by a TFCM because they were discovered after arrival.
choices.C: They are returned to the AECO for amendment of the CIFCM and are then cleared in the normal course.
choices.D: They are considered unmanifested and subject to seizure proceedings.

level2.reason: Under Sec. 8.4, cargoes not listed in the IFCM must be covered by a supplemental IFCM submitted within six (6) hours upon arrival of the aircraft. The cartons were covered 7.5 hours after arrival (2:00 PM to 9:30 PM), so under Sec. 8.5 they are considered unmanifested and subject to seizure proceedings. The twenty-four-hour period in Sec. 8.3.2 applies to the e-CIFCM, not to supplemental IFCMs.

level2.question: A Low-Value, Dutiable express shipment of dietary supplements valued at Php32,000 has a Goods Declaration lodged in the E2M. During review, the customs examiner finds that the supplements require a permit from another regulatory agency, which the AECO has not submitted. The examiner updates the SAD and enters the findings in the Inspection Act. What should the appraiser do, and what follows if the AECO never submits the permit?

choices.A: Re-route the Goods Declaration to Red; if the permit is not submitted, the examiner recommends the issuance of a WSD.
choices.B: Re-route the Goods Declaration to Yellow; if the permit is not submitted, the examiner recommends the issuance of a WSD.
choices.C: Re-route the Goods Declaration to Yellow; if the permit is not submitted, the system automatically assesses the shipment after six (6) hours.
choices.D: Re-route the Goods Declaration to Green; if the permit is not submitted, the examiner recommends the issuance of a WSD.

level2.reason: Under Sec. 13.1.5(a), the appraiser re-routes the selectivity color to Yellow when additional permits, licenses or clearances from other regulatory agencies are required (Red is for physical examination). Under Sec. 13.1.7, if the declarant fails to submit the required documents, the examiner recommends the issuance of a Warrant of Seizure and Detention (WSD).

level2.question: Harbor Express, an AECO, has posted a bank guaranty of Php5,000,000 through an Accredited Agent Bank. Shipments with assessed duties and taxes totaling Php4,950,000 were already released prior to payment and remain unpaid. A new informal-entry shipment valued at Php38,000 has been duly processed and examined, its assessed duties and taxes of Php120,000 are determined, it is not subject to any alert or hold order, and the AECO has submitted the AAB's notarized commitment. May the District Collector release this shipment prior to payment?

choices.A: Yes, because its value is below Php50,000 and the other requirements are complied with.
choices.B: Yes, and the excess of Php70,000 will simply be deducted from the security deposit by the Bureau if the AECO later defaults on payment.
choices.C: No, because only shipments valued at less than Php10,000 may be released prior to payment.
choices.D: No, unless the AECO first increases the security deposit, because shipments not covered by it cannot be released.

level2.reason: Under Sec. 16.3, only shipments whose aggregate assessed duties, taxes and charges do not exceed the amount guaranteed by the AAB may be released. Php4,950,000 + Php120,000 = Php5,070,000, which exceeds the Php5,000,000 guaranty by Php70,000. Under Sec. 6, the AECO must increase the security deposit, otherwise the District Collector shall not allow release of shipments not covered by it.

level2.question: Swiftline, an AECO, receives Express Shipments in Manila at 8:00 AM on Monday that are intended for transshipment to Tokyo by air. The shipments are not exported until Thursday, and no valid cause for the delay is shown. What is the consequence for Swiftline under CMO 09-2021?

choices.A: It can no longer use the longer period to submit the TFCM or OFCM, and it is liable for fines under Section 1412 of the CMTA both as carrier and as consolidator.
choices.B: The shipments are converted to Low-Value, Dutiable shipments, and Swiftline must pay the corresponding duties and taxes under an informal entry before they may be exported.
choices.C: The shipments are treated as abandoned, and the ACDD must dispose of them not later than six (6) months from the Decree of Abandonment.
choices.D: Swiftline must re-export the shipments within ninety-six (96) hours from arrival using a Special Permit to Load.

level2.reason: Under Sec. 21.1.8, Express Shipments for transshipment must be exported within forty-eight (48) hours from arrival. Monday 8:00 AM plus 48 hours is Wednesday 8:00 AM, so Thursday is late. Without a valid cause for extension, the AECO can no longer avail of the longer timeframe for the TFCM or OFCM, is deemed to have failed to submit on time, and is liable for fines under Section 1412 of the CMTA as carrier and as consolidator. The 96-hour period applies only to re-exportation by sea (Sec. 21.1.9).

level2.question: A package arrives whose Air Waybill lists a consignee address in the Philippines, but its labels clearly show a destination in Vietnam, which the assigned Warehouseman verifies. The package is not subject to any alert order, and non-intrusive inspection shows it is not regulated, restricted or prohibited. The AECO notifies the District Collector that the package is mis-sorted only after it has lodged a Goods Declaration for it, and plans to return it to the shipper within 24 hours using a Special Permit to Load. May it be returned without payment of duties, taxes and other charges as a mis-sorted shipment?

choices.A: Yes, because the labels clearly show a foreign destination and the Warehouseman verified it.
choices.B: Yes, because it will be returned to the shipper within 24 hours using a Special Permit to Load.
choices.C: No, because the District Collector was not notified prior to the arrival of the shipment and lodgment of the Goods Declaration.
choices.D: No, because the Air Waybill lists a consignee address in the Philippines, and the labels cannot override the address stated in it.

level2.reason: Sec. 24.1 allows return without payment only if all listed conditions are met. Sec. 24.1.2 accepts an AWB with a Philippine address if the labels clearly show a foreign destination and the Warehouseman verified it, and the conditions on alert orders and the 24-hour return are satisfied (Secs. 24.1.4 and 24.1.5). However, Sec. 24.1.3 requires that the District Collector be notified prior to arrival and lodgment of the Goods Declaration, which was not done here.

level2.question: A typhoon forces an AECO flight bound for Manila to divert to Clark, and the aircraft can no longer proceed to Manila. The AECO had already pre-lodged goods declarations at the Manila port, and transfer of the goods to Manila by land is not possible because of flooded roads. What may the AECO do?

choices.A: Request cancellation of the pre-lodged goods declarations and relodge them at the port of discharge, but only after obtaining clearance from the AOCG.
choices.B: Request cancellation of the pre-lodged goods declarations and relodge them at the port of discharge, without needing clearance from the AOCG.
choices.C: Treat the goods as mis-sorted or misrouted shipments and return them to the shipper within twenty-four (24) hours.
choices.D: Treat the goods as transshipment cargo and export them within forty-eight (48) hours from arrival.

level2.reason: A flight diversion due to inclement weather is an exceptional circumstance beyond the AECO's control (Sec. 20.1). Under Sec. 20.2.1, the AECO may request cancellation of the pre-lodged goods declaration at the port of destination and relodge it at the port of discharge as long as transfer by land is not possible, and clearance from the AOCG is no longer required.

level2.question: A courier package arrives under an AECO's MAWB. The HAWB describes the contents as personal items of no commercial value and states a declared value of Php800 for customs purposes only. The AECO asks for immediate release of the package as an Express Shipment. How should the package be treated?

choices.A: It is not entitled to immediate release; the specific value of the goods must be declared, supported by an available invoice, receipt or equivalent document.
choices.B: It is entitled to immediate release because its value is below the Php10,000 de minimis ceiling.
choices.C: It is entitled to immediate release because a specific amount is stated, even though it is qualified by the phrase for customs purposes.
choices.D: It is not entitled to immediate release, and it must be processed as a high-value shipment under the regular customs cargo clearance procedures once an invoice is submitted.

level2.reason: Under Sec. 18.1, importations declared as of no commercial value, or with a specific amount qualified by the phrase for customs purposes, are not entitled to immediate release as Express Shipments. The same section requires the specific value to be declared, supported by an available invoice, receipt or equivalent document. The low amount does not matter, and high-value processing (Sec. 14) does not apply to a Php800 declaration.

level2.question: A detailed CIFCM covers 40 envelopes in a sealed green courier bag. Non-intrusive scanning flags one envelope, and the examiner, with an AECO representative present, physically inspects it and finds non-document merchandise inside. What may be done with the remaining 39 envelopes?

choices.A: They must wait until the segregated envelope is fully examined and a decision on a WSD has been made.
choices.B: They may be released only after the entire CIFCM is returned to the AECO and an amended CIFCM is approved by the customs appraiser upon the examiner's recommendation.
choices.C: Their processing and release may continue once the AECO applies to amend the CIFCM by splitting it, and the Bureau approves the amendment within twenty-four (24) hours.
choices.D: They must be refiled by the AECO as informal entries using the individual air waybill of each envelope.

level2.reason: Under Sec. 11.11, when the physical examination is positive, the examiner segregates the particular Correspondence or Document but allows processing and release of the cleared items upon receipt of the application for amendment. Under Sec. 11.12, the amendment splits the CIFCM into one for cleared items and one for segregated items, and the Bureau approves it within twenty-four (24) hours from receipt. Only the segregated item, if eventually released, needs a goods declaration using its individual Air Waybill (Sec. 11.13).
